newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan nuclear firm admits radiation warning delay.
newsitem.headline: Japan nuclear firm admits radiation warning delay.

text.p: The operator of the nuclear fuel reprocessing plant that was the site of Japan's worst nuclear accident admitted on Friday that there was a five-hour delay in informing authorities that there had been a radiation leak from the facility.

The state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) said in a report that officials at the Tokaimura nuclear processing plant, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo, waited five hours on March 11 before telling the firm's headquarters in the capital that radiation had leaked after an explosion rocked the plant.
A spokesman said the main reason for the delay was that the ensuing fire at the facility had kept workers from the scene.
The PNC has said measurements made since the accident showed the leaked radiation never reached levels that were harmful to humans or the environment.
The PNC report to the Science and Technology Agency, which stopped sort of identifying the exact causes of the accident pending further investigations, did not explain the reason for the delay.

PNC officials said the fire at the facility, where nuclear waste is mixed with asphalt for long-term storage, may have been caused by a chemical reaction between an acid compound and a solvent which normally never come into contact.
The room at the Tokaimura complex where the fire and an explosion occurred was still too contaminated by radioactivity for investigators to enter, PNC officials said.

The accident exposed 37 workers to radiation and revealed major safety flaws in the country's nuclear power industry, including outdated fire fighting equipment and delays in alerting authorities and nearby residents.
Since the accident the workers have been given a clean bill of health and are back at work.

But the revelations of the lapses have complicated the Japanese government's efforts to restore public trust in its nuclear power programme, which suffered a serious blow last year when PNC officials attempted to cover up an accident at a prototype fast-breeder reactor in western Japan.
